uy-07Np.title: Direction sign: thick white wooden post
uy-07Np.summary: Thick wooden signposts, usually painted white, often with up to four rectangular notches at the back. Bolivia has thick wooden posts too.

uy-0wFk.title: Pole: trident, three upward insulators
uy-0wFk.summary: A very common pole with three insulators pointing up like a trident. The same type exists in the neighbouring Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul.

differs.how: Only in the far south of Brazil, next to the border

uy-3qgY.title: Kilometre marker: green-painted stone
uy-3qgY.summary: A stone kilometre marker painted green. Unique here.

uy-8hZX.title: Landscape: tallest hills in two spots
uy-8hZX.summary: The highest hills are in two areas: near Minas, east of the capital, and north of Tacuarembó in the far north. Use subtle height differences to region-guess.

uy-B0c6.title: Coverage: smudgy picture quality
uy-B0c6.summary: Much of the coverage looks somewhat smudgy. Argentina has this much less often.

uy-CX3t.title: Houses: tall modern flats by a sandy beach
uy-CX3t.summary: A rich seaside resort town with many tall modern apartment blocks and a big sandy beach. Further out are expensive villas and tall pine trees.

uy-D8A0.title: Landscape: very flat southeast near Brazil
uy-D8A0.summary: The southeast near Lagoa Mirim and the Brazil border is very flat, unlike the gentle hills in most of the country.

differs.how: Same flat land continues across the border

uy-E7Gs.title: Google car: white front, curved black back
uy-E7Gs.summary: A unique off-road trekker in Valle del Lunarejo park, west of Tranqueras. The car has a white front and curved black back with a brown strap, on a small track through grassland. The park shows as a point on the map, not a green area.

uy-FChw.title: Plants: short stocky palm trees
uy-FChw.summary: Short, stocky palm trees are an occasional sight.

uy-HRMl.title: Guardrail: small reflector, 3.5-sided support
uy-HRMl.summary: A small rectangular yellow or red reflector, as in Argentina. Tell them apart by the support: Argentine ones have three sides of a rectangle, Uruguayan ones also have bits of the fourth side at the corners.

differs.how: Support has exactly three sides of a rectangle

uy-MSWj.title: Plants: tree plantations
uy-MSWj.summary: Planted tree blocks are common in the countryside, densest in two areas in the north and northwest, with isolated ones all over.

uy-Pveh.title: Bollard: white post, one side yellow
uy-Pveh.summary: White bollards, often with one side painted yellow, and stone barriers. Both are specific to this country.

uy-Ql63.title: Coverage: limited, mostly main roads
uy-Ql63.summary: Coverage is thin. The densest is in the south around the capital; elsewhere it follows the yellow main roads, so guessing the road angle can get you very close.

uy-RpLA.title: Landscape: tall hills with darker soil
uy-RpLA.summary: In the north, tall hills with noticeably darker soil, natural vegetation and often tree plantations. No bare rocks like in the Minas hills. Strongest near the Brazil border on Route 30 near Tranqueras.

differs.how: Brazilian side looks similar, so check signs and plates

uy-VOt5.title: Plate: plain white, black characters
uy-VOt5.summary: Plain white plates with black characters. Argentine plates are also white but have a black dot in the middle or a blue bar on top.

differs.how: Argentine plates have a black dot or a blue top bar

uy-Z9bh.title: Road lines: yellow-white or plain white
uy-Z9bh.summary: Two other patterns that are not unique: yellow-white lines (also in Argentina) and simple white lines (found in many places).

uy-ZQG4.title: Road lines: yellow double with white dashes
uy-ZQG4.summary: Triple road lines: a double yellow line with white dashes between. Not seen anywhere else in the Americas.

uy-Zjpu.title: Landscape: dense big-city sprawl
uy-Zjpu.summary: The capital is by far the biggest city; over half the population lives in its area. If you are somewhere very dense and built-up, guess the capital, since few places elsewhere look like that.

uy-cpJZ.title: Pole: flat metal sheets top or square concrete
uy-cpJZ.summary: Round poles topped with flat metal sheets, and square concrete poles, are both good clues. You may also see simple wooden poles with one insulator and, very rarely, Argentine-style poles.

differs.how: Argentine poles are rare here and look different

uy-grPh.title: Landscape: grassland, gentle hills, overcast
uy-grPh.summary: Open grassland with gentle hills, often under overcast skies, with the odd block of planted trees. Roads are in worse shape than in neighbouring countries.

uy-gxV0.title: Houses: boxy concrete, drab, flat roofs
uy-gxV0.summary: Many houses are cube-shaped concrete with drab, weathered colours and often flat roofs. Argentine houses often look similar.

uy-hQj8.title: Landscape: lots of cattle
uy-hQj8.summary: Cattle outnumber people about four to one, so you see plenty of them in the countryside.

uy-lQlm.title: Soil: reddish, light pink to deep red
uy-lQlm.summary: Reddish soil, from light pink to deep red, is common. It is rarer in similar parts of Argentina, so it helps in a tough call. White and brown soil also occurs, so its absence rules nothing out.

differs.how: Reddish soil is less common there

uy-mVth.title: Landscape: subtle hills, never flat
uy-mVth.summary: Most of the country is slightly hilly even though it's low. Roads usually have at least a slight incline, but the hills are subtle. If it's totally flat, think Argentina.

differs.how: Argentine pampas can be completely flat

uy-mv5R.title: Google car: black car, no antenna
uy-mv5R.summary: Only older Gen 3 coverage, shot by a black car with no antenna. The car is not always visible. Argentina and Peru used the same car.

uy-nX58.title: Road: divided highway
uy-nX58.summary: Divided highways are rare and all near the capital: Ruta 1 west to Colonia Valdense, Ruta IB east to Punta del Este and a short bit of Ruta 5 north to Canelones.

uy-prxs.title: Bins: orange lids
uy-prxs.summary: Bins with orange lids are only in Rocha Department. Black bins appear in both Rocha and Canelones.

uy-qHa3.title: Google car: orange strap on the left
uy-qHa3.summary: A unique off-road trekker in the coastal town of Cabo Polonio, with an orange strap on the left. It passes makeshift-looking shacks by the sea and sometimes drives on the beach.

uy-rYkI.title: Chevron: yellow with black arrows
uy-rYkI.summary: Yellow chevrons with black arrows, like most of Latin America. Useful mainly to rule out Argentina, which uses white with red arrows.

differs.how: Argentine chevrons are white with red arrows

uy-sGGa.title: Landscape: tall hills, exposed rocks, bushland
uy-sGGa.summary: Around Minas are some of the tallest hills here with lots of bare rock and heavy bushes. Usually more subtle than the example. Bare rock is always a good clue. The Quebrada de los Cuervos reserve further north can look similar.

uy-xQPs.title: Coverage: small island trekker, lighthouse
uy-xQPs.summary: Isla de Flores, a small island off the capital, has a walking-camera trek showing abandoned buildings and usually the lighthouse.
